text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- State expects to earn some 30 to 50 billion francs from planned privatisation of France Telecom.

-- Head of CDR structure selling off Credit Lyonnais assets, Michel Rouger, wants all sales to be implemented by March 1998. Out of 197 billions transferred in 1995, 133 billion were still held by the CDR at end 1996.

-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe plans further cut in social charges on low wages in 1998, to cost the state between four and six billion francs, financed by savings on job creation subsidies. Plan is to be presented to the European Commission next week. Charge reduction to be between 1,168 and 2,200 francs at the level of the Smic minimum wage.
-- France Telecom posts a 2.1 billion franc profit for 1996, expects a 14.5 billion franc profit for 1997. It is to launch its partial privatisation on May 6.

-- Finland expected to issue 2008 French-franc bond in April, coupon and maturity in line with equivalent French government bond (OAT). French bank Societe Generale could be added to list of Finnish primary dealers.
-- France Telecom to be listed on Paris and New-York exchanges from June 9, the first tranche is expected to be worth up to 50 billion francs.
-- CDR head Michel Rouger calls for privatisation of remaining CDR assets before 1998 elections.

-- Air France chairman Christian Blanc says he will resign if the company's pilots maintain a strike warning for March 23 to 26, which in his eyes puts the company in jeopardy in a context of tough economic competition.

-- A meeting of Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer with Belgian union leaders yesterday over plans to close a Renault assembly plant in Belgium came to a dead end as Schweitzer said decision remains "irrevocable".
